knife: A knife is a tool that cuts.
He ate with his knife and fork.
A knife is a tool with a thin edge.
He worked with a putty knife.
If you knife someone, you stab someone with a knife; you make a hole in them.
The gang knifed him sixteen times.
knowledge: Knowledge is information that you know.
He shared his knowledge with you.
knee: Part of the leg between the thigh and the shin.
I hurt my knee in football.
To hit someone or something with the knee.
He kneed me in the leg.
knot: A knot is formed when a rope is tied.
He put a knot in the rope.
A knot is a unit of speed.
To create a tied place in a cord or rope.
They knotted the ends of the rope together.
know: When you know something, you have facts or ideas in your mind.
You know a person, if you have met him or her.
Yes, I know John. I met him in class last week.
knock: A sound from something hard hitting wood.
When you knock on something, you hit your knuckles onto it repeatedly.
She knocked on my door three times before I opened it.
When you knock something, you hit it, often accidentally.
known: If something is known, people know about it; it is famous.
It is a known fact that water freezes at 0°C.
In algebra, a variable or constant whose value is already determined.
Any fact or situation which is well-researched or familiar.
knowledgeable: If a person is knowledgeable that person knows many things, or a great amount about something.
She is very knowledgeable when it comes to medicine.
knocker: A knocker is something that knocks or is used to knock.
I used the knocker on the door.
Man, she has a hot set of knockers.
knowing: A knowing look or smile tells someone that you know something.
All set. Have a good weekend," she said with a knowing smile.
knick-knack: A knick-knack is a small item or ornament that is not worth much.
knowingly: If you do something knowingly, you know you are doing it.
It was not an accident -- he knowingly installed a virus in our computer.
If you act knowingly, you show that you know something.
He looked at me knowingly, and I knew he was not fooled.
kneel: If you kneel, you lower your body and put one or two of your knees on the floor.
In many religions, people kneel when they pray.
knight: A knight was a man who fought in battles on a horse during the .
The knights rode up to the castle and broke in.
A knight is a person who has been given knighthood by a king or queen.
, A chess piece, often in the shape of a horse's head, that is moved two squares in one direction and one at right angles to that direction in a single move, leaping over any pieces in between.
knead: When you knead, you press a mixture of flour and water with the hands to make bread.
knit: When you knit, you make a cloth from a long wool thread, usually by hands with needles.
My mother loves to knit beautiful scarves for me to wear.
knob: A knob is a rounded handle on a door or drawer.
knuckle: A knuckle is the joint of a finger, especially the bottom joint of a finger.
knobs: In the game of cribbage, knobs is the Jack of the same suit as the card that was revealed after the deck was cut.
knickers: Knickers refers to the underwear (a piece of clothing) that is worn by a female.
knoxville: Knoxville is a town in United States of America. It is located in Tennessee state.
knotty: A knotty problem or issue is complicated and difficult to solve.
Nobody can agree about how to deal with this extremely knotty problem.
kneadable: If something is kneadable, it can be kneaded.
knowledgable: If a person is knowledgable that person knows many things, or a great amount about something.
She is very knowledgable when it comes to medicine.
knack: If you have a knack for doing something, you have a special skill or ability to do it easily.
He has a knack for fixing computers.
A knack is a trick or a clever way of doing something.
The door sticks, but there's a knack to opening it.
knockoff: A knockoff is an imitation of a well-known product. It is usually of poorer quality and cheaper than the original.
kneecap: A kneecap is the round bone that covers and protects the knee joint.
She fell and bruised her kneecap while running.
If you kneecap someone, you injure their kneecap, often by shooting or hitting it.
The gang threatened to kneecap him if he didn’t pay.
knitter: A knitter is a person who makes clothing or other items by knitting yarn with needles.
knavish: A knavish person is someone who is dishonest and sly.
